blocks.text: `docker events` is the daemon's timestamped stream of lifecycle events (oom, kill, die, restart, health_status); disk exhaustion comes mainly from build cache, unused images, logs and writable layers.

$ docker events --filter container=rag-api-1 --since 30m
... container oom      (name=rag-api-1)
... container kill     (signal=9)
... container die      (exitCode=137)
... container restart
$ docker events --filter event=die --format '{{.Actor.Attributes.name}} {{.Actor.Attributes.exitCode}}'
The backlog is limited; ship events to your logging stack for history.

items: `no space left on device` in builds.
Containers fail to start; logs stop.
`df -i`: inode exhaustion gives the same errors with free space left.
Docker Desktop: the VM disk has its own cap.

blocks.text: Q: "How do you find out what happened to a container at 3 a.m.?" A: "docker events for the sequence (oom → kill → die → restart) with timestamps, docker inspect for the final state, docker logs around that time, and the host kernel log to confirm OOM kills."

items: Build cache and logs are the usual disk hogs.
